overview: The Council recapped recent outreach events, reviewed progress on municipal energy reduction goals, and discussed the status of pending city tree ordinances. Members also began planning for a potential local job fair in partnership with regional workforce agencies.

items.title: Administrative Business
items.summary: Approval of the previous meeting's minutes was postponed until the next session.

items.title: Future Meeting Schedule
items.summary: The Council scheduled a hybrid meeting for December 16 and moved the January meeting to January 27 via Zoom to accommodate the Martin Luther King Jr. Day holiday.

items.title: Winter Preparedness Event Recap
items.summary: Members discussed the success of the coat and hat distribution at City Hall, noting high attendance and the benefits of using the City Council chambers for public events.

items.title: Upcoming Community Events
items.summary: The Council reviewed plans for the Winter Extravaganza on December 4 and an Electrify Medford coaching event at the library on January 16.

items.title: Electrify Medford and Energy Aggregation
items.summary: Brenda Pike reported that 92 residents have signed up for coaching and highlighted new electricity aggregation pricing that will automatically save some residents significantly on their utility bills.

items.title: Green Communities Annual Report
items.summary: Municipal energy use has decreased by 19% from the 2009 baseline, though officials noted the reduction is partially attributed to warmer winters.

items.title: Energy Committee and Zero Waste Initiative
items.summary: The Energy Committee is seeking new members and exploring a zero-waste program involving swap events and recycling improvements for local restaurants.

items.title: Air Quality and Extreme Weather Communications
items.summary: In response to recent wildfire smoke, the group reviewed real-time air quality mapping tools and discussed developing standardized tips for various extreme weather events.

items.title: Tree Ordinances and Landmark Trees
items.summary: The City Council Committee of the Whole will review public and private tree ordinances on November 20, while Trees Medford works to identify historically significant landmark trees.

items.title: Tree Care and Community Service
items.summary: Members discussed the intensive watering requirements for new city trees during the current drought and suggested involving students in local tree maintenance projects.

items.title: Job Fair Planning
items.summary: The Council proposed a partnership with MassHire and ABCD to host a job fair in Medford, specifically targeting green jobs and career opportunities for the migrant community.

items.title: Transportation and Bus Route Changes
items.summary: Members discussed pending MBTA bus route redesigns scheduled for 2025 and planned to distribute translated information to impacted residents.
